newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gold closes steady, silver gains.
newsitem.headline: Indian gold closes steady, silver gains.

text.p: ** Gold 24 carat closed 10 rupees higher at 4,850 rupees per
10 gramme against the previous close of 4,840 rupees as
fresh seasonal buying drove market upward after a steady
start
** Silver (.999) closed 15 rupees higher at 7,095 rupees per
kg against previous closing of 7,080 rupees on the back
of a shortage of ready stock and speculative support
which drove prices upward after easy start. Silver was up
by 55 rupees per kg on Saturday.
TODAY'S CLOSING (BOMBAY) PVS CLOSING
Gold 24 carat 4,850 rupees per 10 gms (+10) 4,840
Silver.999 7,095 rupees per kg (+15) 7,080

Gold 24 carat closed 10 rupees higher at 4,850 rupees per 10 gramme against the previous close of 4,840 rupees on the back of fresh seasonal buying which drove prices upward while limited supplies kept offerings at a low ebb, dealer said.
Gold was up by 40 rupees per 10 gramme on Saturday.
Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closed 100 rupees higher at 56,700 rupees per piece after a gain of 500 rupees on Saturday. They were up by 1,100 rupees per piece during last week.

Silver (.999) on the other hand closed 15 rupees higher at 7,095 rupees per kg against the previous close of 7,080 rupees as thin supplies and shortage of ready stock helped the market to bounce back after easy start when market opened five rupees lower at 7,075 rupees per kg. Silver was up by 55 rupees per kg on Saturday and by 275 rupees during last week.

Overall market sentiments for both the precious metals remained firm during the day but in the evening traders were predicting higher prices to attract profit-taking looking at the modest setback in the world market after recent rally. (Conversion $1=35.84 rupees)
